valuation_philosophy.model_type: Blended AFFO-capitalization / NTA-based cost-of-equity model (REIT), NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Property For Industry is an internally-managed, NZX-listed pure-play Auckland industrial REIT (90+ properties, NZ$2.30bn portfolio at a 5.7% cap rate, 98.7% occupancy, WALT 5.04yrs, gearing 34.2%). Reported NPAT and statutory EPS are dominated by IAS-40 fair-value revaluation noise -- FY2026 EPS fell 21.11 to 15.47cps purely because the fair-value gain shrank ($70.7m FY2025 vs $16.1m FY2026) while AFFO per share ROSE 14.0% -- so P/E and EPS growth are explicitly excluded as valuation drivers. The valuation base is company-disclosed AFFO (FFO less maintenance capex and incentives), which is measured AFTER interest expense: it is an equity-level cash flow, capitalized at the COST OF EQUITY, and net debt is NEVER subtracted from the resulting value -- doing so would double-count leverage already embedded in AFFO. The reported FreeCashFlow column (OCF less capex, structurally negative) is not used: REIT cash-flow-statement capex is overwhelmingly discretionary acquisition/development spend (FY2026 -113.5m recorded, understated further by a $19.4m non-cash land settlement), not a cost of running the standing portfolio. Per NZ-REIT house precedent (ARG.NZ, IPL.NZ, PCT.NZ), the final value blends 50/50: (1) a 5-year AFFO-per-share projection capitalized at cost of equity with a Gordon terminal exit yield, and (2) projected NTA per share at a justified exit P/NTA plus the PV of interim cash dividends. FY2026 AFFO of 10.93cps contains ~1.02cps of one-off GrainCorp lease-surrender income ($5.12m recognised as rental income); the FY2027 base-year AFFO of 10.30cps is instead anchored to management's own FY2027 guidance (9.75-9.85cps dividend at ~95% AFFO payout), which nets that one-off out. The blended base-case value of ~$2.05 vs the $2.37 price is an honest 'fully priced at our required return' conclusion: the market prices PFI at an implied ~7.3-7.5% cost of equity (P/AFFO 21.7x, P/NTA 0.82x), below our 8.6% requirement -- PFI is a quality hold for income, not a buy at this price.

warnings: REIT AFFO-capitalization + NTA model, not an owner-FCF/WACC DCF. Statutory NetIncome/EPS are IAS-40 fair-value noise (FY2021 +$452.8m profit, FY2022 -$13.9m and FY2023 -$97.8m losses on cap-rate expansion) and drive nothing here.
AFFO is already post-interest (equity-level). Net debt (NZ$799.2m incl. $19.4m deferred settlements) is NEVER subtracted from any value in this model -- doing so would double-count leverage.

FY2024 is a SIX-MONTH transition stub (six months to 30-Jun-2024, balance date change Dec->Jun). It is excluded from every CAGR, P/AFFO and EV/EBITDA calculation; only its balance-sheet P/NTA is used.
FY2026 AFFO of 10.93cps includes ~1.02cps of one-off GrainCorp surrender income; the base year is normalized via FY2027 guidance-implied AFFO of ~10.3cps rather than growing the reported figure.

TotalDebt (782.0m) is borrowings only; NZ$19.4m of deferred acquisition settlements are debt-like and added to net debt for EV computations. FY2026 recorded cash capex (-113.5m) also understates economic capex by the $19.4m non-cash land settlement.
~95% AFFO payout leaves minimal retained capital; the $325-350m development pipeline is debt/recycling funded, taking gearing toward ~35.7% (target band 30-40%, covenant <50%).
Terminal/exit value is 72-78% of both legs' value -- the valuation is primarily a statement about exit yield and exit P/NTA; see sensitivity matrix.

Base-case IV implies P/NTA of ~0.71x, slightly BELOW the 8-year FY-end band (0.77-1.33x). This is not a model error: it is the direct consequence of requiring an 8.6% equity return where the market has historically accepted ~7.3-7.5%. The NTA leg (exit 0.85x) already anchors half the value to market-evidence pricing. Direction of error is conservative, not manufactured upside.

inputs.model: AFFO capitalization at cost of equity, 50/50 blended with NTA exit-multiple leg (NZ REIT house method)
inputs.notes: Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: REIT / property trust row -> AFFO capitalization at cost of equity, never subtract net debt. Consistent with ARG.NZ, IPL.NZ, PCT.NZ, NZL.NZ precedents. Fresh build -- no prior PFI.NZ DCF exists.
inputs.share_count_basis: Closing shares on issue 30-Jun-2026 (FY2026 annual report); share count essentially flat since FY2018 (498.7m -> 502.4m); no SBC dilution issue (StockBasedComp immaterial, $0.85m H1 FY2026)
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings 782.0m + deferred acquisition settlements 19.4m (debt-like, excluded from TotalDebt) - cash 2.15m. Used ONLY for EV/EBITDA cross-checks; never deducted in the valuation (AFFO is post-interest).
inputs.affo_normalization_note: FY2026 AFFO includes NZ$5.12m (~1.02cps) one-off GrainCorp lease-surrender payment recognised as rental income (Aug-2025). Normalized FY2026 AFFO ~9.91cps.
inputs.fy2027_affo_basis: FY2027 dividend guidance midpoint 9.80cps at management-implied ~95% AFFO payout -> ~10.3cps
inputs.sbc_source: Internally managed REIT; long-term-incentive share scheme immaterial (H1 FY2026 StockBasedComp $0.85m ~ 1.5% of AFFO); no SBC adjustment needed and share count held flat -- stated explicitly, not silently skipped
inputs.last_fcf_note: No owner-FCF figure is used -- AFFO is the valuation base, capitalized at cost of equity. Reported FreeCashFlow (OCF-capex) is structurally negative because capex is discretionary development/acquisition spend.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-25T17:00:08+12:00 NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime; verified live, not stale)

historical_growth.balance_date_note: FY2018-FY2023 are Dec-31 twelve-month years; FY2024 is a SIX-MONTH stub to 30-Jun-2024; FY2025/FY2026 are Jun-30 twelve-month years. All CAGRs computed on like-for-like spans EXCLUDING the stub (FY2018->FY2023 = 5.0yrs, FY2023->FY2026 = 2.5yrs, FY2018->FY2026 = 7.5yrs). Any CAGR spanning FY2024 as if it were a full year is meaningless.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward AFFO-per-share growth (base case): through-cycle AFFO/share CAGR was 5.2% (FY2018-26 span) but the recent 8.5% (FY2023-26) is flattered by the FY2026 GrainCorp one-off; 4.0% reflects reversion capture (~7.1% under-rented) plus development completions net of higher funding costs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Statutory EPS 'growth' is meaningless (fair-value noise: EPS swung 89.97 -> -2.76 -> -19.48 -> 21.11 -> 15.47cps while AFFO/share compounded smoothly at 3.6-5.2%). Equity/NTA CAGR is likewise revaluation-dominated (NTA +71% FY2018-21 on cap-rate compression, -11% FY2021-23 on expansion) and is not used as a growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: AFFO per share is the only clean compounding series. FY2026 revenue growth (+13.3%) is flattered by the $5.12m surrender payment and acquisition timing.

cost_of_equity_build.risk_free_rate_note: NZ 10-year government bond, midpoint of 4.2-4.5% range
cost_of_equity_build.beta_note: Defensive industrial landlord: near-full occupancy through the cycle (98.6-100% every year since 2018), 5-year WALT, diversified 120+ tenant base, ~80% hedged debt -- but levered ~34% LVR, so above a pure unlevered property beta
cost_of_equity_build.geographic_concentration_note: ~85-88% of portfolio value in a single city (Auckland); a regional shock hits PFI harder than diversified peers
cost_of_equity_build.premiums_not_applied: No small-cap illiquidity premium (NZ$1.19bn market cap, NZX-50 constituent, NZDX bond issuer); no governance/external-manager premium (internally managed since 2017, lowest MER among NZ listed property); no tenant-concentration premium (largest tenants single-digit % of rent)
cost_of_equity_build.market_implied_check: At $2.37 the market prices PFI at ~4.6% forward AFFO yield + ~3% growth = ~7.3-7.5% implied cost of equity; our 8.6% requirement is deliberately more demanding, which is why the base IV sits below the price.

assumptions.wacc_rationale: Not a WACC model: AFFO is post-interest, so the discount rate is the levered COST OF EQUITY built above (NZD flows discounted at an NZD-based rate: NZ 10yr rf + NZ ERP). Debt cost (4.64% weighted average, ~80% hedged) enters through the AFFO projection, not the discount rate.

base.affo_growth_rationale: FY2027 ~10.3cps from guidance (net of the surrender one-off; +3.9% on normalized FY2026 9.91cps). FY2028-31: rent reversion (~7.1% under-rented, ~7.8%/yr of contract rent reaching expiry/review) + Springs Rd/Harris Rd/Spedding Rd development completions at 15-20% margins, partly offset by funding costs as gearing rises to ~35.7% and hedges roll; tapering 4.5% -> 3.5%
base.nta_growth_rationale: Matches FY2025->FY2026 actual (+2.3%): retained AFFO (~0.5cps) + development margin (~2-2.5cps/yr on ~$65m spend) + market-rent-driven revaluation at stable 5.7% cap rates
base.exit_p_nta_rationale: Between the post-2022 rate-normalized band (0.77-0.83x, avg 0.80x) and the 8-year average (0.95x); assumes modest normalization above today's 0.82x as the OCR cutting cycle completes, well below the 2019-20 low-rate peaks (1.19-1.33x)

bull.affo_growth_rationale: Full reversion capture, speculative space (Springs Rd Stage 2) leases quickly, OCR cuts flow through the ~2.3yr hedge book, development pipeline accelerates at 15-20% margins
bull.exit_p_nta_rationale: Market paid 0.98-1.33x NTA in 2018-2021 easing cycles; 1.0x is the conservative end of that regime

bear.affo_growth_rationale: NZ recession: occupancy slips to ~96-97%, reversion stalls, Springs Rd Stage 2/Harris Rd sit vacant longer, hedge roll-off raises debt cost despite OCR cuts, tax depreciation removal bites
bear.nta_note: ~50-75bp cap-rate expansion drives valuation losses roughly offsetting rental growth (echo of FY2022-24: NTA fell 303 -> 271cps)
bear.exit_p_nta_rationale: Below the post-2022 minimum FY-end print (0.77x), consistent with a rate-shock trough

nta_based_leg.methodology: PV of interim cash dividends at cost of equity + PV of year-5 NTA/share x justified exit P/NTA. No net-debt deduction -- NTA is already post-debt book value.

entry_price.basis: AFFO-capitalization leg only, per NZ-REIT house formula (IPL.NZ precedent): interim AFFO and scenario terminal value discounted at the 15% hurdle. No net-debt adjustment (AFFO post-interest). A 15% hurdle is deliberately punishing for an income REIT -- the entry price answers 'at what price is PFI a 15%/yr investment', not 'what is it worth'.

sensitivity.matrix_note: AFFO-capitalization leg only, base AFFO path held constant. Rows = cost of equity (7.6-9.6%), columns = exit AFFO yield (4.85-6.85%). $/share.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20/55/25 bear/base/bull. Bear held at 20% (vs house 15% default): the downside is cap-rate/rate-cycle re-rating, not solvency (gearing 34.2% vs <50% covenant, ~80% hedged, staggered NZDX/USPP maturities) -- but rate sensitivity is PFI's single largest risk and FY2022-24 showed a real -11% NTA drawdown. Bull at 25%: FY2027 dividend guidance is already issued, occupancy 98.7%, and the reversion+development pipeline gives genuine upside optionality.

sanity_check.note: REIT model: earnings multiples use AFFO per share, not GAAP EPS (statutory EPS is fair-value noise). EBITDA here is rental EBITDA (operating income excl. fair-value movements, per Metrics CSV) so EV/EBITDA IS computable for PFI, unlike some IAS-40 peers, and is used as a third check. FY2024 six-month stub excluded from P/AFFO and EV/EBITDA (flow-based); its P/NTA retained (balance-sheet based). EV uses net debt including the $19.4m deferred settlements. Historical prices are FY-end month closes: Dec for FY2018-23, Jun for FY2024-26 (balance-date change).

historical_multiples.p_nta_note: 2019-2021 prints (0.98-1.33x) belong to the ultra-low-rate era; the post-2022 rate-normalized band is 0.77-0.83x

implied_multiples_at_current_price.p_e_note: Skipped: statutory EPS is fair-value-distorted (15.47cps FY2026 vs 21.11 FY2025 purely on revaluation size) and not a valuation-relevant multiple

trip_thresholds.upside_trip: upside >100% while price in upper half of 10yr range -- N/A: base upside is NEGATIVE (-13.5%), so the overvaluation trip cannot fire

sanity_check.diagnosis: No overvaluation trip: every implied multiple at the base IV (P/NTA 0.71x, P/AFFO 18.7x reported / 19.8x normalized, EV/EBITDA 16.9x) is BELOW its historical average and maximum. The one flag runs the OTHER way: implied P/NTA of 0.71x sits ~8% below the 8-year FY-end minimum (0.77x). Diagnosed cause: the model requires an 8.6% cost of equity while the market has persistently priced PFI at ~7.3-7.5% (P/AFFO 22-37x, P/NTA 0.77-1.33x across the cycle). This is a deliberate return-requirement gap, not a broken assumption -- the NTA leg (exit 0.85x, calibrated to PFI's own trading history) already anchors half the valuation to market-evidence pricing, and the FY2027 base year is management's own guidance-implied AFFO. Conclusion stands: fully priced at our required return; the market's price embeds a lower one.
